maria: Bringing up orison7b-lite (int3) on Dedicated — seeing a weird 'vocab shear' where some tokens shift in long-context summaries. Quick heads-up.

sasha: Can you paste a tiny repro (prompt + output) and what converter/quant toolchain you used? :thinking_face:

maria: Prompt:
```
System: Summarize the article below.
Article: The council approved a policy that affects remote work and tax rules for contractors.
```
Converted (int3) output: "The council approved a policy that changes taxes for contractors working remotely, which ..."  — some proper nouns get replaced or shifted (e.g., "contractors" -> "contractor s").
Toolchain: rwd-convert v0.9.2 + quant-int3-exporter (internal).

ben: This smells like quadphase rotary packing + tokenid aliasing. Our int3 exporter packs rotary params headwise and we saw head-shifts in kvcache before (see bug #1428). If the tokenmap also had an off-by-one, small drift amplifies in long context.

eva: Try conversion with `--rotary-mode=phasefold` and apply the tokenmap shim (tokenmap=surface->bpe) during export. Phasefold remaps quadphase packing to canonical ordering we use in runtime.

maria: Good call. Quick eval numbers: Wikitext-103 ppl +1.15, news-summarize ROUGE-L down ~0.6 on our smoke set (100 docs). Latency/throughput fine. Looks like quality regression not perf.

ben: Short reproducer checks:
1) inspect vocab ids around the problematic tokens: `python -m rwdn.tools.inspect_vocab --model out/orison_int3 --range 480-520`
2) dump kvcache tokenids for the run and compare with float32 baseline.

ci-bot: conversion-smoke: test_longctx_align FAILED (1/5) — mismatch metric=0.0042, logs at gs://ci-conversion/orison/6112233445

sasha: If phasefold fixes it, also run a tiny AB eval (n=200) comparing int3-phasefold vs int3-default on summ-qa and codegen to make sure no regressions in other workloads.

maria: I ran the phasefold conversion locally; pushing logs to gs://ri-onboard/maria/orison-int3/phasefold-try. Will trigger CI AB and post results. Thanks :thumbsup:
